Towards the start of the Third Age, a great freeze took hold of Ebos. The Dendra flew out in all directions and upon their return, it was confirmed: All of Ebos was experiencing winter. The weather and seasonal patterns they had observed for millennia were no longer valid. Crops and herds died, but The Dendra were thankful to see how quickly the forest adapted. The Tannsgrisnirs grew thick striped coats, mushrooms could be cultivated in heaps of warm decomposing materials (a process that was also utilized to warm the glass rooms) and their dormant fruit and nut trees were quickly overtaken by vines of a golden berry, whose sweet juice was often fermented into a crisp Winter Wine.

For twenty years the Dendra waited for the world to change back, all while attempting to explain the long winter or find some observable pattern, but there was nothing. A fear spread that the Third Age would be known only as the Age of Ice and Snow, and that children born in this time would know only the freeze.

In the thousands of years since their Creation, the Dendra had known peace, health and abundance, which allowed them to leisurely study and create. This strange new time was bringing about hardships and forcing innovations. They would need to branch out from their forests in ways they never had before, seeking assistance and trade from whatever other sentient beings they came across.

They hoped that the other creatures of Ebos would recognize their dire need for fellowship.

Where I am going with this is that the Dendra have lived in comfort for thousands of years, just relaxing and studying and flying, writing books about the natural sciences and developing simple medicines. They’ve had no need to branch out – but that is changing.
Soon after Silvano took the appearance of a fallen Dendra, the “Ice Age” began on Ebos. His nomadic Vaal offspring would now be around 20 years old. The bloodline of Dendra he started with his woman, thousands of years ago, still has their own family tree, but not everyone has the shifting gene and those who do have kept it secret.
Over the past several thousand years they’ve invented paper and writing products, agriculture and natural sciences, and simple clothing, armor and weaponry. I can add Savagery if anyone reading this thinks it’s necessary. :)
